Nearly every throne in Europe in 1914 traced back to the same handful of German castles and Italian towns. One family basically ran the continent.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Trace royal bloodlines to their origin points and the map collapses toward Central Europe: Britain's House of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, Russia's Holstein-Gottorp-Romanovs, and Habsburgs, Hohenzollerns and Savoys all radiating from tiny German and Italian towns.
2/ Britain's own royal family was, by 1914, dynastically German — the House of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, named for a small duchy. It was renamed 'Windsor' in 1917 purely to sound less German during WWI.

3/ Russia's ruling house traces to Holstein-Gottorp, a duchy on the Danish-German border, via an 18th-century marriage. The 'Romanov' name survived even after the bloodline was genetically almost entirely German.
4/ The Habsburgs ran an empire from a single castle in modern Switzerland — Habsburg castle, built around 1020 — before relocating their power base to Austria centuries later.

5/ King George V of Britain, Tsar Nicholas II of Russia, and Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany — the three monarchs who took Europe into WWI in 1914 — were first cousins, all grandsons or grandsons-in-law of Queen Victoria.

6/ A war that killed millions was, at the top, partly a family quarrel between cousins whose thrones all trace back to the same small patch of Central Europe.

Which royal bloodline surprised you most? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
